body.anaDetail: No AI provider is configured. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or OPENAI_API_KEY / KIMI_API_KEY) — without one, every AnA turn returns 503 GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE.

steps.title: The sign-in page takes the user into the shell
steps.action: Open /concept2cure/login unauthenticated. Credentialed run (VALIDATION_USER_PASSWORD set): enter email and password, then the current authenticator code when the server asks for it. Development run: click "Demo Access". Observe the redirect into the shell
steps.expected: Login page renders; after sign-in the URL leaves /concept2cure/login and the shell renders
steps.observed: signed in with password + authenticator code; landed on /concept2cure
steps.note: On a server that is not a development one, every password login is answered with an MFA challenge and there is no dev-login; the credentialed branch signs in the way a person does. Demo Access calls POST /api/auth/dev-login, which only a development server with ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1 answers (server/auth/dev-auth-policy.ts); it skips the password and MFA factors by design.

steps.title: Program creation validates its inputs
steps.expected: Both refused with HTTP 400 and a message naming the field
steps.observed: missing name → 400 ({"error":"name is required"}); bad type → 400 ({"error":"programType must be one of: 510k, de_novo, pma, ivd, device, cer, ide, ind, cta, bla, biologic, nda, maa, jnda, anda, mdr, ivdr, dmf"})

steps.title: Create an IND program
steps.expected: HTTP 201; data.id is a UUID; the row carries the given name; meta reports what else the intake created (scaffolded document, canonical submission)
steps.observed: program d9bcbda0-3c11-4f6c-b50e-555be08bc961 created (ws=Biotech, code=OIP2-YYC0); intake also created: document=doc_e7c6e13089004477bbb4b0fb3899dd83 (92 sections), submission=49; projectAnchor=NO_CLIENT_WORKSPACE

steps.title: Program is listed and readable for the organisation
steps.expected: List contains the new program; detail returns the same name
steps.observed: listed (44 programs) and readable; product class shown as "biologic"

steps.title: Program creation is attributable in the activity feed and the hash-chained audit log verifies
steps.expected: Activity has ≥1 entry for the creation with an actor and time; the audit_logs chain verifier answers ok

steps.title: Program creation appears on the organisation audit ledger surface
steps.expected: At least one hash-chained entry exists for the organisation after a program was created, and the server's chain verdict says the chain verifies (meta.chain.ok = true)
steps.observed: ledger entries: 50 (50 hash-chained); server chain verdict ok=true over 325 row(s); newest: {"id":"AUD-9e0e1f5d-1027-4db6-8a64-719baec7eb3a","when":"2026-09-23 04:34","at":"2026-09-23T04:34:03.267Z","actor":"OQ Runner","event":"C2c Project Create","tar
steps.note: The ledger surface reads audit_logs, where program intake writes its chained row (server/routes/c2c/projects.ts), merged with audit_events (server/routes/audit-trail-ledger.routes.ts). v0.1 counted entries only, so an unchained entry or a broken chain passed; the step now checks what its expected result says.

steps.title: Projects surface renders the program
steps.expected: The program name is visible on the page

steps.title: Project home renders for the open program
steps.action: Open /concept2cure/project-home with the program selected in the shell
steps.expected: Project home renders with the program name and no runtime page error

steps.title: Create a task and see it on the task board
steps.expected: Task created (2xx) with a taskId; the board lists it
steps.observed: task TASK-1790138057956-4f7e49d9 created and listed (board total 14)

steps.title: Program journey read model answers
steps.expected: HTTP 200 with data[] (empty is honest for a new program)

steps.title: Filings catalog surface renders
steps.expected: Surface renders (screenshot) without a runtime page error

steps.title: Launch scope is enforced in the navigation verdicts
steps.expected: launchScope.enforced=true; the out-of-scope surface "rbm" is not entitled with source "launch-scope"; all six launch apps' primary surfaces are entitled
steps.observed: 101 verdicts; rbm locked by launch-scope; launch surfaces entitled

steps.title: Deep link to an out-of-scope surface shows the launch-scope gate
steps.expected: The page explains the surface is not in this release (no RBM content, no upsell)

steps.title: A program id the organisation does not own is not readable
Every sign-in attempt is entered in the organisation audit trail
steps.action: Credentialed run: POST /api/auth/login with a wrong password; POST /api/auth/login with the password, then POST /api/auth/mfa/verify with a wrong code; POST /api/auth/login with the password, then POST /api/auth/mfa/verify with the current authenticator code. Then GET /api/audit-trail/ledger?limit=50
steps.expected: HTTP 401; 200 then 401; 200 then 200 with a session. The ledger then holds exactly five entries for the run identity that it did not hold before the step, reading newest first, each hash-chained: "Signed in: password and second factor verified", "Password verified: authenticator code requested", "Second factor refused: wrong code", "Password verified: authenticator code requested", "Sign-in refused: wrong password"; the server chain verdict is ok
steps.observed: sign-in statuses 401, 200, 401, 200, 200; 5 new ledger entries for user:17, newest first: "Signed in: password and second factor verified", "Password verified: authenticator code requested", "Second factor refused: wrong code", "Password verified: authenticator code requested", "Sign-in refused: wrong password"; all hash-chained; server chain verdict ok=true over 331 row(s)
steps.note: Every sign-in outside development is challenged, and each of its events names the user organisation, which the pre-auth scope every /api/auth request runs in could not write under RLS (VSR-001 §13, F-19): the trail was empty and no step saw it. The sign-in calls go straight to the server, not through the recorded API client, so no password or code reaches the record; the observed result carries their statuses. A dev-login run passes through none of these events, so it is a deviation.

steps.title: Signing out ends the session
steps.action: Open a session of the step's own for the run identity (password and authenticator code on a credentialed run; dev-login on a development run). GET /api/c2c/projects with it; POST /api/auth/logout with it; then, with the same token, GET /api/c2c/projects and GET /api/auth/session. Read the ledger (GET /api/audit-trail/ledger?limit=50) with the run session before and after
steps.expected: Projects 200 before; logout 200; afterwards the projects API answers 401 and the session check authenticated=false. The newest ledger entry the step added for the run identity reads "Signed out", hash-chained
steps.observed: own session (password+totp): projects 200; logout 200; afterwards projects 401, session check signed out; newest new ledger entry for user:17: "Signed out", chained
steps.note: The step signs out a session of its own, so the run's session stays open for the steps after it. Until AUTH-03 was fixed (VSR-001 §13.9, F-21) logout answered "Tokens invalidated." and the token went on opening the API, the session check and the collaboration socket for the rest of its 24 hours.
